12570-starr-of-the-desert.title: Starr Of The Desert
12570-starr-of-the-desert.creator: Unknown
12570-starr-of-the-desert.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Peter finished refilling the prescription on which he was working, and went out to see if he were needed in front. He sold a lip-stick to a pert miss who from sheer instinct made eyes at him, and he wished that Helen May had such plump cheeks--though he thanked God she had not the girl's sophisticated eyes.

arxiv-2106-02236.title: Refined clock-jitter reduction in the Sagnac-type time-delay interferometry combinations
arxiv-2106-02236.creator: Pan-Pan Wang 1, Yu-Jie Tan 1, Wei-Liang Qian 1,2,3, Cheng-Gang Shao 1
arxiv-2106-02236.description: Abstract The ongoing development of the space-based laser interferometer missions is aiming at unprecedented gravitational wave detections in the millihertz frequency band. The spaceborne nature of the experimental setups leads to a degree of subtlety regarding the otherwise overwhelming laser frequency noise. The cancellation of the latter is accomplished through the time-delay interferometry technique.

arxiv-2106-09350.title: Identifiability of AMP chain graph models
arxiv-2106-09350.creator: Yuhao Wang, Arnab Bhattacharyya
arxiv-2106-09350.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yuhao Wang, Arnab Bhattacharyya. We study identifiability of Andersson-Madigan-Perlman (AMP) chain graph models, which are a common generalization of linear structural equation models and Gaussian graphical models. AMP models are described by DAGs on chain components which themselves are undirected graphs. For a known chain component decomposition, we show that the DAG on the chain components is identifiable if the determinants of the residual covariance matrices of the chain components are monotone non-decreasing in topological order.

arxiv-2112-04835.title: Depth of Binomial Edge Ideals in terms of Diameter and Vertex Connectivity Thanks: AMS Subject Classification (2020): 13D02, 13C13, 05E40
arxiv-2112-04835.creator: A. V. Jayanthan, Rajib Sarkar
arxiv-2112-04835.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A. V. Jayanthan, Rajib Sarkar. Let G G be a simple connected non-complete graph and J G J_{G} be its binomial edge ideal in a polynomial ring S S . arxiv-2310-10096.title: LLP-Bench: A Large Scale Tabular Benchmark for Learning from Label Proportions
arxiv-2310-10096.creator: Anand Brahmbhatt*, Mohith Pokala*, Rishi Saket, Aravindan Raghuveer
arxiv-2310-10096.description: Abstract In the task of Learning from Label Proportions (LLP), a model is trained on groups (a.k.a bags) of instances and their corresponding label proportions to predict labels for individual instances. LLP has been applied pre-dominantly on two types of datasets - image and tabular.

arxiv-2402-09038.title: Tunneling of quantum geometries in spinfoams
arxiv-2402-09038.creator: Pietro Donà, Hal M. Haggard, Carlo Rovelli, Francesca Vidotto
arxiv-2402-09038.description: Abstract Quantum gravitational tunneling effects are expected to give rise to a number of interesting observable phenomena, including, in particular, the evolution of black holes at the end of their existence or the emergence of the early universe from a quantum phase.

arxiv-2406-03058.title: Higher order approximation of nonlinear SPDEs with additive space-time white noise
arxiv-2406-03058.creator: Ana Djurdjevac, Máté Gerencsér, Helena Kremp
arxiv-2406-03058.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ana Djurdjevac, Máté Gerencsér, Helena Kremp. We consider strong approximations of 1 + 1 1+1 -dimensional stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise. It has long been proposed [ DG01 , JK08 ] , as well as observed in simulations, that approximation schemes based on samples from the stochastic convolution, rather than from increments of the underlying Wiener processes, should achieve significantly higher convergence rates with respect to the temporal timestep. The present paper proves this.

arxiv-2503-09081.title: Everything Can Be Described in Words: A Simple Unified Multi-Modal Framework with Semantic and Temporal Alignment
arxiv-2503-09081.creator: Xiaowei Bi, Zheyuan Xu
arxiv-2503-09081.description: Abstract While multi-modal learning has advanced significantly, current approaches often create inconsistencies in representation and reasoning of different modalities. We propose UMaT, a theoretically-grounded framework that unifies visual and auditory inputs as structured text for large language models, addressing semantic alignment, temporal synchronization, and efficient sparse information retrieval. It significantly improves state-of-the-art Long Video Question Answering accuracy (up to 13.

arxiv-2503-15945.title: Preparing for Rubin-LSST - Detecting Brightest Cluster Galaxies with Machine Learning in the LSST DP0.2 simulation
arxiv-2503-15945.creator: A. Chu, L. Doeser, S. Ding, J. Jasche
arxiv-2503-15945.description: Abstract The future Rubin Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) is expected to deliver its first data release in the current of 2025. The upcoming survey will provide us with images of galaxy clusters in the optical to the near-infrared, with unrivalled coverage, depth and uniformity.

arxiv-2508-19379.title: Robust Recursive Query Parallelism in Graph Database Management Systems
arxiv-2508-19379.creator: Anurag Chakraborty, Semih Salihoğlu
arxiv-2508-19379.description: Abstract . Efficient multi-core parallel processing of recursive join queries is critical for achieving good performance in graph database management systems (GDBMSs). Prior work adopts two broad approaches. First is the state of the art morsel-driven parallelism, whose vanilla application in GDBMSs parallelizes computations at the source node level.

arxiv-2509-03492.description: Abstract The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (Roman) will conduct a Galactic Exoplanet Survey (RGES) to discover bound and free-floating exoplanets using gravitational microlensing. Roman should be sensitive to lenses with mass down to ∼ 0.02 ​ M ⊕ \sim 0.02\;M_{\oplus} , or roughly the mass of Ganymede.

pmc-10681917.title: Quantitative microbiological risk assessments for Salmonella spp. contaminated taiwanese salty chicken in the taiwanese population
pmc-10681917.creator: Keng-Wen Lien, Meng-Xuan Yang, Min-Pei Ling, Guo-Jane Tsai
pmc-10681917.description: The aim of the study is to develop Salmonella spp. Quantitative microbial risk assessments (QMRA) and to evaluate the risk of Salmonellosis illness in the Taiwanese population after consumption of Taiwanese salty chicken (TSC). We assume that Salmonella spp. May contaminate the fresh raw chicken used in TSC.

pmc-10744777.title: Investigation and Tailoring of Rotating Squares’ and Rectangles’ Auxetic Structure Behavior through Computational Simulations of 6082T6 Aluminum Alloy Structures
pmc-10744777.creator: Mahmoud Elsamanty, Hassan Elshokrofy, Abdelkader Ibrahim, Antti Järvenpää, Mahmoud Khedr, Reza Hedayati
pmc-10744777.description: Auxetic structures, renowned for their unique lateral expansion under longitudinal strain, have attracted significant research interest due to their extraordinary mechanical characteristics, such as enhanced toughness and shear resistance. This study provides a systematic exploration of these structures, constructed from rigid rotating square or rectangular unit cells.

pmc-11364271.title: Microbiological performance and adherence in blood culture protocols: The role of a second anaerobic bottle
pmc-11364271.creator: Paula C Vergara, Cristian García, Melissa Accini, Liliana Franco, Johanna M Vanegas, Santiago Atehortúa
pmc-11364271.description: BackgroundBacteremia represents high rates of morbidity and mortality, especially in developing countries, highlighting the need for a diagnostic method that allows prompt and appropriate patient treatment. This study compared microbiological performance and adherence of two blood culture protocols for the diagnosis of bacteremia.MethodsQuasi-experimental study conducted between June 2022 and February 2023. Two blood culture protocols were evaluated.

pmc-11508510.title: Reanimation Techniques of Peripheral Facial Paralysis: A Comprehensive Review Focusing on Surgical and Bioengineering Approaches
pmc-11508510.creator: Carmelo Saraniti, Barbara Verro, Michael J Brenner
pmc-11508510.description: Peripheral facial paralysis represents a disabling condition with serious psychological and social impact. Patients with peripheral facial paralysis have a disfigurement of the face with loss of harmony and symmetry and difficulties in everyday facial functions such as speaking, drinking, laughing, and closing their eyes, with impairment of their quality of life.

pmc-11716902.title: Association between anticholinergic burden and volumes of the basal forebrain and hippocampus across the Alzheimer’s disease spectrum ‐ data from the DELCODE study
pmc-11716902.creator: Ingo Kilimann, Jonas Peltner, Fedor Levin, Annika Spottke, Oliver Peters, Emrah Düzel, Frank Jessen, Britta Haenisch, Stefan Teipel
pmc-11716902.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundDrugs with desirable and undesirable anticholinergic effects influence cognitive performance and increase the risk of dementia later in life. MRI imaging studies showed structural effect of these substances on basal forebrain and hippocampus, key regions of Alzheimer’s disease pathology.MethodsWe analyzed data from 787 participants of the DELCODE study with a diagnosis of subjective cognitive impairment (SCD), mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease dementia, 1st degree relatives of people with dementia and cognitively healthy controls.

pmc-12444626.title: Electrochemical insights into manganese–cobalt doped α-Fe2O3 nanomaterial for cholesterol detection: a comparative approach
pmc-12444626.creator: Sushmitha S, Subhasmita Ray, Lavanya Rao, Mahesha P. Nayak, Karel Carva, Badekai Ramachandra Bhat
pmc-12444626.description: Herein, a self-assembled hierarchical structure of hematite (α-Fe2O3) was synthesized via a one-pot hydrothermal method. Subsequently, the nanomaterial was doped to obtain MxFe2−xO3 (M = Mn–Co; x = 0.01, 0.05, and 0.1) at precise concentrations. An electrode was fabricated by coating the resulting nanocomposite onto a nickel foam (NF) substrate.

pmc-12839165.title: MASLD or MetALD? Unveiling the Role of Alcohol in Liver Disease Progression in Diabetic Patients
pmc-12839165.creator: Ermina Stratina, Carol Stanciu, Robert Nastasa, Sebastian Zenovia, Remus Stafie, Adrian Rotaru, Stefan Chiriac, Irina Girleanu, Cristina Muzica, Horia Minea, Laura Huiban, Anca Trifan
pmc-12839165.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: The transition from the term non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) to steatotic liver disease (SLD), an umbrella term for several related conditions, offers benefits, particularly in identifying cardiometabolic risk factors more effectively. However, the impact of alcohol consumption on liver disease progression remains significant, leading to the recognition of a new entity: MetALD (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with moderate alcohol intake).

pmc-13102882.title: Quasi-randomization to Cannabinoid Condition in Studies of US Legal Market Cannabis: Characteristics of Accepters Versus Decliners of Condition Assignment
pmc-13102882.creator: Carillon J Skrzynski, Angela D Bryan, Sarah J Schmiege
pmc-13102882.description: Although random assignment is the standard for drawing causal inferences within clinical trials, it is generally precluded in legal market cannabis research given its federal classification as a schedule 1 drug. Unfortunately, this may cause selection bias and compromise internal validity, and thus, alternative approaches are necessary.

pmc-13658192.title: Multiscale structural connectome eigenmodes constrain human brain functional dynamics
pmc-13658192.creator: Jie Xia, Siqi Yang, Jinpeng Niu, Xinyue Huang, Jiao Li, Huafu Chen, Fang Zeng, Wei Liao
pmc-13658192.description: The human brain is an intricate network structurally organized across multiple scales. Multiscale structural architecture arises from complex biological mechanisms and provides the anatomical substrate for functional interactions. However, the extent to which the multiscale structural connectome constrains functional activity remains unclear.
